title: Stop the first edit of every wiki page from conflicting

blocks.text: A team wiki keeps its pages in a table whose `updated_at` column holds epoch milliseconds. To stop two people from overwriting each other, every edit carries the `updated_at` of the version it was made from, and the store refuses the edit if that is no longer the current version.
`PageStore` creates, reads and saves pages, and it reads time from the `Clock` it is given. Finish its two `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/PageStore.java`:

items: `stamp()`: the moment recorded as a new version's `updated_at` and returned to the client;
`isCurrent(...)`: whether a client's stamp names the version the column holds.

blocks.text: When you're done, a client can edit a page with the stamp it got from `create`, `read` or `save`, and an edit made from a replaced version is refused, however soon after the replacement it arrives. About two lines in total.
The tests drive the store with a clock they move by hand, and its readings carry nanoseconds.

cases.says: an edit made from the version just read is saved, and a later edit made from that same, now replaced, version is refused
the stamp handed back by create still matches the column, so the first edit goes through
two versions saved 300 ms apart get different stamps
an edit made from a version that was replaced less than a second ago is refused, not saved over the newer one

origin.section: A Timestamp Survives a Store Only at the Store's Precision

concepts: Truncating stamps further than the store needs, to seconds, gives two versions in the same second the same stamp, so a stale edit passes the check.
An instant written to a millisecond store and read back is unequal to the original unless it was truncated to milliseconds when stamped.
